evidence.claim: A role provider can replace another provider's credential and then lower its expiry by calling grantRole twice: first with an expiry slightly later than the current one (passing the newExpiry > oldExpiry check), then again with a shorter expiry (allowed because it is now the previous provider).

missing.item: Demonstration that the lowered expiry produces a concrete harm beyond the lender's credential expiring earlier (e.g. lender locked out of withdrawal/transfer, or funds stranded), given that known-lender status (isKnownLenderOnMarket) is set on first deposit/transfer and persists independently of credential expiry.
missing.why: The stated effect is only that a provider can lower another provider's expiry. Because known lenders retain withdrawal/transfer rights regardless of credential state (onQueueWithdrawal/onTransfer check isKnownLenderOnMarket first), the report does not show the expiry reduction actually denies any in-scope action or causes loss, so the impact/severity is unsupported.
missing.resolves_when: A concrete scenario is shown where the shortened expiry blocks a specific market action or causes asset loss for a lender who is not a known lender, or the impact is restated as a pure access-control/credential-integrity issue with matching severity.

missing.item: Confirmation that the borrower adding a malicious/compromised role provider is not the excluded condition; i.e. whether the attack requires a provider the borrower chose to trust.
missing.why: The path requires an approved role provider acting against another provider's grant. evidence.claim: Delinquency status is only computed in _writeState after state updates, so a market that becomes delinquent via accrued interest/withdrawal processing is not flagged delinquent until the end of the tx, letting the borrower dodge the penalty APR by topping up reserves just before a withdrawal is processed.

blocking.why: _writeState recomputes isDelinquent from updated state and totalAssets() at end of every state-changing call, so the flag is never stale after a tx.
_getUpdatedState accrues interest/fees and processes batches before _writeState; delinquency is evaluated on the resulting state, not skipped.
Interest/fee accrual uses updateScaleFactorAndFees with delinquencyFeeBips and grace period, which is what actually determines penalty APR, independent of the isDelinquent flag.

missing.item: Demonstration that a market can accrue base-only interest (no penalty) for a period while actually delinquent, i.e. that the grace tracker/timeDelinquent is not advanced by updateScaleFactorAndFees.
missing.why: The stated impact (lenders lose delinquency fee) requires the penalty accrual to be bypassed; the code shows penalty accrual is driven by FeeMath, not the isDelinquent flag, so without this the effect is unsupported.
missing.resolves_when: A test or trace shows timeDelinquent/grace tracker not incrementing across a delinquent interval, or a concrete loss of penalty interest.

missing.item: Concrete call sequence with values showing the borrower's top-up avoids a penalty that would otherwise have accrued.
missing.why: The report gives only a narrative; no numbers or executed test show the penalty is actually avoided rather than merely the flag being set at tx end.
missing.resolves_when: A runnable test or step-by-step trace with amounts and timestamps shows penalty APR avoided.

missing.item: Policy basis for treating borrower reserve top-ups as an attack rather than the documented trusted-borrower behavior.
missing.why: The policy lists borrowers as trusted and states the fundamental assumption that assets are returned to honor required reserves; the described 'exploit' is exactly that behavior, so reachability under allowed actors is not established as a bug.
missing.resolves_when: A cited policy clause or invariant showing reserve top-ups to avoid delinquency are out of bounds.

evidence.claim: Delinquency status is only computed in _writeState after _getUpdatedState accrues interest/processes withdrawals, so a market that becomes delinquent due to accrued interest is not flagged delinquent and lenders miss penalty interest; borrower can front-run/repay to dodge penalty.

blocking.why: _writeState recomputes isDelinquent from current liquidityRequired() vs totalAssets() on every state write, so the flag is never stale after a state-touching call.
_getUpdatedState accrues interest/fees and processes batches, then callers call _writeState which sets isDelinquent; the two are not decoupled as claimed.

missing.item: Demonstration that the residual debt after repayOutstandingDebt() is not simply the correct, expected interest accrual on outstanding (unpaid) debt, i.e. that the borrower is charged more than the true debt owed at the time of repayment.

If the residual is just legitimate interest on unpaid debt, the 'repayment ineffective / borrower pays more' impact does not hold and severity collapses to informational. The claim needs a case where the borrower overpays relative to the debt actually owed at repayment time (e.g. double-counting of pending withdrawals or fees).
missing.resolves_when: A test shows that after repayOutstandingDebt() the borrower has transferred more than the market's true debt (principal + accrued interest up to that block), or that totalDebts()-totalAssets() after repayment exceeds interest accrued on the remaining outstanding principal over the elapsed time.
